bug_description.original: A vulnerability exists in the idn2_to_ascii_4i() function where the output length is not restricted to 63 characters.
bug_description.normalized: The staged 52-byte witness passes the fuzzer's `(size & 3) == 0` gate, allocates a 64-byte `out2` buffer, and feeds the same 13 raw UCS-4 words through six constant `flags[it]` values into `idn2_to_ascii_4i`. On the loop iteration that crashes, `idn2_lookup_u8` first normalizes that flag value with `set_default_flags`, runs `_tr46`, copies the processed UTF-8 result into `_mapped`, and then builds an ASCII lookup name from `_mapped` while checking only the 255-byte `IDN2_DOMAIN_MAX_LENGTH` bound. The saved ASan run proves that one such iteration returns a 65-byte NUL-terminated lookup string to `idn2_to_ascii_4i`; that function then checks only `rc == IDN2_OK` and `output != NULL`, never enforces the documented 63-character output limit, and `strcpy` writes 66 bytes into the 64-byte heap buffer. Because the crash occurs inside the six-entry flag loop, the staged artifacts do not identify which `flags[it]` arm produced the successful lookup.

source.description: First project-code statement that consumes the attacker-controlled UCS-4 words by copying `inlen` elements from the fuzzer-provided `input` pointer into libidn2's internal `input_u32` buffer on the selected loop iteration.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is exactly 52 bytes, so the fuzzer's `(size & 3) == 0` gate passes and the loop at `fuzz/libidn2_to_ascii_8z_fuzzer.c:72-73` calls `idn2_to_ascii_4i((uint32_t *) data, size / 4, out2, flags[it])` with 13 raw 32-bit words and six constant flag values. The exact crashing `flags[it]` arm is not recovered from the saved artifacts, but each iteration receives the same 13 words, including two little-endian `0x0000002E` code points, before `_tr46` remaps them inside `idn2_lookup_u8`.
source.note: This step materializes the fuzzer bytes as libidn2-owned UCS-4 data for the later UTF-8 conversion and lookup path.

tainted_value_origin.code: uint8_t *tmp = (uint8_t *) malloc (lookupnamelen + 1); if (tmp == NULL) return IDN2_MALLOC; memcpy (tmp, _lookupname, lookupnamelen + 1); *lookupname = tmp;
tainted_value_origin.description: After `_tr46` remaps the input and the label loop appends admitted label chunks into `_lookupname`, `idn2_lookup_u8` allocates `lookupnamelen + 1` bytes, copies the accumulated ASCII lookup name, and returns that heap string via `*lookupname`. On the staged crash, ASan's `WRITE of size 66` shows this returned lookup name is 65 bytes long.

root_cause.description: Immediately before the copy site, the only remaining gate is that the caller supplied a non-null `output` pointer. There is no `strlen(output_u8) <= 63` check even though the comment directly above states that the caller buffer must have room for at least 63 characters plus the terminator.
root_cause.note: The patch fixes exactly this obligation by inserting `size_t len = strlen ((char *) output_u8);` and returning `IDN2_TOO_BIG_DOMAIN` when `len > 63`, before `strcpy` executes.

sink.description: ASan sink. `strcpy` copies the returned lookup string into the caller's fixed 64-byte heap buffer. On the staged witness the copy spans 66 bytes, so the 65-byte ASCII domain plus terminator overruns that allocation.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 66` at `lib/lookup.c:621`, and the allocation stack points to the fuzzer's `malloc(64)` at line 67 for the same destination pointer.

parser_admitted.description: The crashing iteration reaches the lookup-name accumulation path and passes the only output-length guard present there: the code limits only the 255-byte total-domain size, not the separate 63-character `idn2_to_ascii_4i` output contract.

tr46_remap_mandatory.description: None of the six harness flag values includes `IDN2_NO_TR46`; after `set_default_flags` the branch remains taken, so `idn2_lookup_u8` always remaps into `_mapped` before any `strchrnul` or `label` processing.

lookup_bound_only.description: The lookup path guards only the 255-byte total-domain limit. Passing this guard on the crashing iteration does not enforce the separate 63-character `idn2_to_ascii_4i` output contract, so the long lookup string still returns to the caller.

coarse_trace.summary: Because the staged 52-byte input is divisible by 4, the fuzzer allocates a 64-byte `out2` buffer and runs the same 13 raw UCS-4 words through `idn2_to_ascii_4i` for six constant flag values.
On the crashing loop iteration, the function copies the attacker-controlled UCS-4 words into internal storage and converts them to a UTF-8 buffer for lookup processing.
The chosen flag value is normalized with `set_default_flags`, then `_tr46` remaps the UTF-8 input and `src` is rebound to `_mapped` before any label splitting or length accounting.
The remapped `_mapped` buffer is processed label by label, appended into `_lookupname` under only the 255-byte total-domain guard, and returned as a 65-byte heap string on the crashing iteration.
Back in `idn2_to_ascii_4i`, the long lookup result is accepted with only `rc == IDN2_OK` and a non-null `output` check; without a 63-byte guard, `strcpy` overflows the caller's 64-byte heap buffer.

fine_trace.note: The staged witness is 52 bytes long, so this gate passes and the fuzzer enters the `idn2_to_ascii_4i` path.
Allocates the fixed 64-byte destination later passed as `output`. ASan identifies this heap region as the overflowed allocation.

fine_trace.code: for (unsigned it = 0; it < sizeof(flags)/sizeof(flags[0]); it++) idn2_to_ascii_4i((uint32_t *) data, size / 4, out2, flags[it]);
fine_trace.note: The harness invokes `idn2_to_ascii_4i` six times with the same 13 raw UCS-4 words and the constant flag values `0`, `IDN2_NFC_INPUT`, `IDN2_TRANSITIONAL`, `IDN2_NONTRANSITIONAL`, `IDN2_TRANSITIONAL|IDN2_USE_STD3_ASCII_RULES`, and `IDN2_NONTRANSITIONAL|IDN2_USE_STD3_ASCII_RULES`. The saved crash proves only that one iteration of this loop reaches the sink; it does not identify which `flags[it]` value it was.

On the selected loop iteration, libidn2 copies the 13 attacker-controlled 32-bit words into owned storage and appends a terminating zero, creating the UCS-4 buffer consumed by the rest of `idn2_to_ascii_4i`.
Converts the copied UCS-4 sequence into a UTF-8 string for lookup processing. This pre-TR46 UTF-8 buffer is the input that `idn2_lookup_u8` later remaps.

fine_trace.code: rc = set_default_flags(&flags); if (rc != IDN2_OK) return rc;
fine_trace.note: Normalizes the selected `flags[it]` value in place. For the six harness constants this call succeeds; `0` and `IDN2_NFC_INPUT` are upgraded to include `IDN2_NONTRANSITIONAL`, and none of the six values includes `IDN2_NO_TR46`, so the later TR46 remap branch remains enabled.

fine_trace.code: rc = _tr46 (src, &out, flags); outlen = u8_strlen (out); memcpy (_mapped, out, outlen + 1); src = _mapped;
fine_trace.note: Before any label splitting, `idn2_lookup_u8` runs `_tr46` on the pre-TR46 UTF-8 buffer, measures the returned string, copies it into `_mapped`, and rebinds `src` to `_mapped`. On the crashing iteration `_tr46` succeeds and the mapped string fits `_mapped`, so later `strchrnul`, `label`, and domain-length checks operate on TR46-processed bytes, not directly on `input_u8` from step 5.

fine_trace.code: const uint8_t *end = (uint8_t *) strchrnul ((const char *) src, '.'); size_t labellen = end - src; rc = label (src, labellen, tmp, &tmplen, flags);
fine_trace.note: The loop now parses the remapped `src` buffer label by label and asks `label()` to turn each label into an ASCII chunk `tmp` of length `tmplen`. The exact remapped bytes and exact crashing `flags[it]` arm are not recovered from the staged artifacts, but the overflowing iteration necessarily takes this path with `label()` returning `IDN2_OK` for each label it processes.

This guard limits only the total lookup name to `IDN2_DOMAIN_MAX_LENGTH` (255 bytes). On the crashing iteration the accumulated output stays within that bound, so the function continues even though `idn2_to_ascii_4i` later copies into a caller buffer documented as needing only 63 characters plus NUL.

fine_trace.code: memcpy (_lookupname + lookupnamelen, tmp, tmplen); lookupnamelen += tmplen; if (*end == '.') { _lookupname[lookupnamelen] = '.'; lookupnamelen++; } _lookupname[lookupnamelen] = '\0';
fine_trace.note: Appends each admitted label chunk, and a dot when `*end == '.'`, into `_lookupname`, incrementally building the ASCII lookup string that will later be returned. The final crashing iteration builds a string long enough that the later `strcpy` copies 66 bytes including the terminator.

fine_trace.code: uint8_t *tmp = (uint8_t *) malloc (lookupnamelen + 1); if (tmp == NULL) return IDN2_MALLOC; memcpy (tmp, _lookupname, lookupnamelen + 1); *lookupname = tmp;
fine_trace.note: After the label loop finishes, `idn2_lookup_u8` materializes the accumulated `_lookupname` in heap storage and returns it via `*lookupname`. The later ASan `WRITE of size 66` at `strcpy` implies that this returned string on the crashing iteration is 65 bytes long plus the terminator.

On the loop iteration that overflows, this call returns `IDN2_OK` and hands `idn2_to_ascii_4i` the heap string from step 11 in `output_u8`. Other iterations in the six-entry harness loop may fail earlier or return different results; the staged artifacts do not distinguish them.

The copy block is now gated only by a non-null caller buffer. Because the fuzzer supplied `out2`, this condition passes, and there is still no `strlen(output_u8) <= 63` check despite the comment directly above documenting that requirement.

ASan sink. `strcpy` copies the 65-byte lookup string plus its terminator into the 64-byte `out2` allocation, producing the recorded heap-buffer-overflow `WRITE of size 66` at the right edge of that heap region.

allocation_context.note: ASan reports the overflowed region as the 64-byte heap allocation made for `out2` at the fuzzer call site.

sanitizer_ground_truth.source: parsed from staged sanitizer_trace.txt, default_crash_trace.txt, reproduction_report.json, patch.diff, and the preserved vulnerable container source

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes. The ASan allocation frame is the fuzzer's 64-byte `out2` buffer, and the trace's sink is the unchecked copy into that exact pointer.
cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch inserts a `strlen(output_u8)` check in `idn2_to_ascii_4i` and returns `IDN2_TOO_BIG_DOMAIN` when the result exceeds 63 characters, preventing the overflowing `strcpy` on the saved witness.

poc.trigger: The staged 52-byte witness takes the `(size & 3) == 0` branch, allocates `out2 = malloc(64)`, and is passed as 13 raw UCS-4 words through the six-entry `flags[]` loop into `idn2_to_ascii_4i`. The saved vulnerable run proves that one loop iteration passes through `set_default_flags`, `_tr46`, and the `_mapped`-based lookup build, returns a 65-byte ASCII string, and `strcpy` then overflows `out2`, reproducing `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 66` at `lib/lookup.c:621`; the exact crashing `flags[it]` value is not identified by the staged artifacts.

format.name: 52-byte raw UCS-4LE blob for `libidn2_to_ascii_8z_fuzzer`
format.contract: Exactly these 52 bytes: `20 20 01 00 20 20 00 00 20 32 00 00 2E 00 00 00 20 32 00 00 FF 00 00 00 20 20 00 00 20 20 01 00 2E 00 00 00 20 32 00 00 20 20 00 00 20 AA 00 00 20 20 01 00`. The fuzzer interprets them directly as 13 little-endian 32-bit words and, because the file length is 52, enters the `idn2_to_ascii_4i` loop with a 64-byte `out2` buffer. That loop tries six constant flag values; the saved vulnerable run proves that one of those iterations passes through `set_default_flags`, `_tr46`, the `_mapped`-based label and lookup-name build, and returns a 65-byte ASCII string that `strcpy` copies into `out2`. This contract is limited to the exact staged witness and observed crash: the staged artifacts do not identify the exact crashing `flags[it]` value or reconstruct the exact returned ASCII text after TR46 remapping.
